clue.text: Nonconformity of odd characters from next door confused with youth

indicators.note: confused says the gathered letters are jumbled together into a new order
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are picked out of the word next

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neighbour's eccentric household and a young person together produce some unconventional behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters from' applies only to 'next', giving NX; 'door' is used whole. NX + DOOR + YOUTH is jumbled by 'confused with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unorthodoxy is a refusal to follow accepted beliefs or practices, which is what nonconformity also describes.

clue.text: Murder victim featured in French article after another died in America, nameless

indicators.note: after says the article with the victim comes after the other article

parts.note: un is another French article, the indefinite one

indicators.note: featured in says the victim sits inside the article

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
Abel was murdered by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: An unnamed murder victim appears in a French newspaper article, after another death in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in America' flags the US spelling with one L in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlabeled carries no tag or label, so it has no name attached.

clue.text: Comply with notice

definitions.meaning: to ... a rule or custom is to comply with it

explanation.definitionFit: Observe means both keeping to a law and perceiving something with the eyes.

clue.text: Person who gets under your skin and makes a lasting impression?

definitions.text: Person who gets under your skin and makes a lasting impression?

parts.words: Person who gets under your skin and makes a lasting impression?
parts.note: taken literally, someone whose needle goes into the skin and leaves a permanent design

explanation.surface: An irritating person who nonetheless leaves a strong memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets under your skin' is an idiom for annoying, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo artist inks designs into the skin with needles, leaving permanent marks.

clue.text: Pervasive character associated with US party lines

indicators.note: lines here means goes inside as a lining, so the party sits within the other piece

parts.note: our means associated with us; the capitals of US are a disguise
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A distinctive character linked to the policy lines of an American political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' is capitalised to look like America but is just 'us'. DO lines OUR: O(DO)UR.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour can mean a pervading quality or aura, as in an odour of sanctity.

clue.text: Fruit loop rants about end of civilisation

parts.note: O is loop-shaped

indicators.note: about says the verb for rants goes round the final letter

parts.note: rages means rants

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of civilisation

explanation.surface: A crackpot fulminates about the collapse of civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit loop' reads as slang for a crank; it is the definition plus the O. RAGES goes about N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits, so the plural noun matches the collective use of fruit.

clue.text: Means of raising votes in favour of parliament's closure

parts.note: yeas are votes in favour

indicators.note: closure means the end, so the final letter of parliament is used

explanation.surface: A way of raising votes for the shutting of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' suggests raising support, but it is bread rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the leavening agent that makes dough rise in baking.

clue.text: Man weighed down by the world taking time off finally

definitions.text: Man weighed down by the world

indicators.note: taking with off says a letter is removed from the phrase meaning finally
off completes taking ... off: the time abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A man crushed by the world's troubles finally takes some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Titan Atlas was made to hold up the heavens, and is pictured carrying the globe on his shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan of Greek myth is traditionally shown bearing the globe on his shoulders as a punishment.

clue.text: We aren't sick, hurt or knocked out

indicators.note: hurt says the letters of the phrase are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest that we are not ill, injured or unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ignores the apostrophe. 'knocked out' means amazed here, not unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knocked out in the informal sense is being overwhelmed with wonder or awe.

clue.text: Strongly criticised adult in accepted role

indicators.note: in says the adult abbreviation sits inside the phrase for accepted a role

parts.note: took part means joined in, accepting a role
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Someone was harshly attacked for the grown-up part they agreed to play.
explanation.definitionFit: To take apart a person or their work is an idiom for criticising it severely and thoroughly.

clue.text: Filter tricky question about school

indicators.note: about says the word for tricky question goes round the school

parts.note: a teaser is a tricky question
to school is to train

explanation.surface: A sieve: a puzzling question regarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is the verb, to train. TEAS(TRAIN)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer is a small sieve that filters loose leaves out of a poured cup.

clue.text: Prohibition era bungled attempt to clip mob's wings

indicators.note: to clip means to grip, as a clip holds something, so these letters enclose the pair from mob
bungled says the letters of era are botched into another order

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters of mob are used

explanation.surface: In the Prohibition era, a botched effort was made to clip the mob's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' turns ERA into EAR; with GO this clips the wings of 'mob', M and B: E(MB)ARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade, so it is a prohibition.

clue.text: Right for one motoring club to hold races in sporting event

parts.note: e.g. (for example) means for one

indicators.note: to hold says the club's letters wrap round the races

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring club
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A motoring club, the proper body for it, hosts races at a sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Britain's Automobile Association) holds TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle races, giving ATTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat or yacht races, a sporting event on water.

clue.text: What has a pronounced effect on El NiÃ±o?

definitions.text: What has a pronounced effect on El NiÃ±o?

parts.words: What has a pronounced effect on El NiÃ±o?
parts.note: the mark over the n in Niño changes how it is pronounced, rather than being a weather influence

explanation.surface: A question about what strongly influences the El Niño weather pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' reads as 'marked', but here means affecting pronunciation: the wavy mark over the n makes it 'ny'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the diacritic over the Spanish ñ, changing its pronunciation.

clue.text: Demanding son lives in temporary shelter outside

indicators.note: outside says the phrase for in a temporary shelter sits around the other pieces

parts.note: in tent means in a temporary shelter
is means lives, exists

explanation.surface: An insistent son is living out in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' looks like a noun but is the verb form IS, as in 'he is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An insistent person keeps pressing a demand, so insistent behaviour is demanding.

clue.text: Concocted plan to serve up great dishes

indicators.note: serve up, in a down entry, says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: mega is slang for great
tarts are pastry dishes

explanation.surface: A cooked-up scheme to present great food.
explanation.walkthrough: MEGATARTS reversed upward reads STRATAGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme devised to outwit someone, a contrived plan.

clue.text: Former political organisation is upset about bombing?

parts.note: ex means former
the PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organisation

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says is is turned over, reading upwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A former political group is distressed by a bombing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a bombing is one kind of explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombing results in a blast, so it is an instance of an explosion.

clue.text: Flasher wearing ripped coat covered with lots of dirt

parts.note: in means wearing, as in dressed in

indicators.note: covered with says the shortened dirt goes round the jumbled coat
lots of, not all, says the last letter of dirt is dropped
ripped says the letters of coat are torn apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A flasher in a torn coat smeared with dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' gives DIR from dirt; 'ripped' turns COAT into CATO, which DIR covers: IN + DI(CATO)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's indicator is the light that blinks to signal a turn, so it is a flasher.

clue.text: Church had gold and property in France

parts.note: ate means had, as in had a meal
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A church once owned gold and land in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' means ate, as in had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French country house or estate, a property in France.

clue.text: Marine creature more likely to bleed when caught

indicators.note: caught here means caught by the ear, heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: seepier means more likely to seep, to leak out like a bleed

explanation.surface: A sea creature that bleeds more readily once it is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like fishing but means heard by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the cuttlefish genus, a marine mollusc that gives its name to the brown ink.

clue.text: Second of two drinks

parts.note: the first of the two drinks: to sup is to drink
the second of the two drinks: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: The second of a pair of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is the verb, to back a motion, not an ordinal. 'two drinks' supplies both pieces together, SUP and PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it formally, so to support it.

clue.text: Takes issue with the idea of making money illegally?

definitions.text: Takes issue with the idea of making money illegally?

parts.words: Takes issue with the idea of making money illegally?
parts.note: issue means children, so the clue describes snatching children for a ransom, not disagreeing

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a scheme for earning money by crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes issue' reads as 'disagrees', but issue means offspring: a criminal takes children to demand ransom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abducts a child for ransom snatches offspring to extort money unlawfully.

clue.text: Parties stopped by King lead to Independence Day?

indicators.note: stopped by says the other letters plug the gap inside the parties

parts.note: dos are parties
R is from Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: lead to means the leading letter of Independence

explanation.surface: Celebrations interrupted by a king bring on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independence Day' reads as the holiday, but Day is the surname of Doris Day, the American singer and actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was the American film star, so Doris is a first name that goes with Day.

clue.text: Smart point that's not particularly precise?

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a compass point
the suffix -ish means roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: A clever point that is rather vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' means stylish here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable and elegant, like a smart outfit.

clue.text: First floor is managed by those in power

parts.note: top means first, at the head
to floor someone is to down them, knock them over

explanation.surface: The first floor is run by the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' looks like a storey but is the verb, to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-down organisation is one directed from the highest level of authority downward.

clue.text: Held back career winning acceptance for disheartened, vulnerable youngster

indicators.note: held back says the word for career is read backwards

parts.note: to career is to run headlong

indicators.note: disheartened says the middle letter, the heart, is taken out

parts.note: selling an idea is winning acceptance for it

explanation.surface: A setback in one's career, then winning acceptance for a dispirited, defenceless young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' reverses RUN to NUR; 'disheartened' removes the middle L of SELLING, leaving SELING.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an infant being nursed, a young child dependent on care.

clue.text: Generally, underwear is filled with this elastic material

indicators.note: the answer is what fills the word for underwear, so its outside letters are discarded

parts.note: hosiery is knitted goods, a general term for underwear and stockings

explanation.surface: Underwear, as a rule, is stuffed with this stretchy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is filled with this' keeps only the inside of HOSIERY, dropping H and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow twig, prized for being pliable and used in basketry.

clue.text: Quiet American politician not backing out blocks major settlement

indicators.note: blocks says out sits inside the letters for quiet, obstructing them

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: backing says the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A quiet American politician who won't support an exit obstructs a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not backing' gives TON. Southampton is a port city on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Southampton is a large English port city, so a major settlement in the sense of a populated place.
